title: Ecommerce Working Capital: How to Fund Your Next Inventory Cycle
summary: Plan ecommerce working capital around inventory, expenses, and sales receipts. Calculate your cash gap and compare financing that fits your operating cycle.
body_markdown:
[Hero photo: The Retro Store / Unsplash. Illustrative order packing in Glasgow.](https://unsplash.com/photos/man-in-black-jacket-holding-brown-cardboard-box-R99qruYcodE)


**Ecommerce working capital** supports the everyday costs of running an online store: inventory, fulfillment, advertising, payroll, and refunds. The amount you need changes with reorder dates, sales speed, and when money reaches your bank account.


A useful **ecommerce working capital** plan follows those cash movements week by week. It helps answer a practical question: can the business pay for its next order while the current stock is still selling?


## What working capital means for an online store


The[SEC defines working capital](https://www.sec.gov/about/reports-publications/investorpubsbegfinstmtguide) as current assets minus current liabilities. Inventory can count as a current asset, but it still needs to sell before it produces cash.


### Profit and available cash follow different clocks


Positive margins can coexist with a temporary cash shortage. **Working capital for ecommerce** has to cover the interval between paying for goods and collecting spendable proceeds, including returns and operating costs.

## Build a weekly cash forecast


Start with unrestricted cash, add expected receipts, and subtract payments by their actual due dates. This turns **online store working capital** into a calendar you can update as orders change.


### Map inventory payments


Record deposits, final vendor payments, freight, duties, and fulfillment intake costs. Review[vendor payment terms](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/vendor-contracts-and-payment-terms) alongside reorder lead times. A reorder can fall due before the previous batch has sold through.


### Include operating expenses


Add payroll, advertising, software, shipping, refunds, taxes, and debt payments. Budget a cash cushion for slower sales or higher returns. **Working capital for online retailers** needs to cover the whole operating cycle.


### Use realistic collection dates


Model when net proceeds are available, allowing for platform deductions, payout timing, and possible reserves. For marketplace-specific mechanics, see the[Amazon seller financing guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/amazon-seller-financing) .


## Calculate the funding gap


Here is an illustrative forecast for one inventory cycle. Assume the business starts with $30,000 available and receives the modeled $45,000 only after the expenses below.


Cash movement Amount


Opening cash $30,000


Inventory payment −$40,000


Freight and duties −$8,000


Operating expenses −$12,000


Balance before sales receipts −$30,000


Later net sales receipts +$45,000


Ending balance $15,000


The business needs **$30,000** to bridge its lowest cash point. Maintaining a separate $10,000 minimum cushion raises the modeled funding need to **$40,000** . Actual results depend on payment sequencing, collections, financing costs, and repayments.

## Match financing to the expense


### Vendor payments


\[Vendor Financing\](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/finance-guides/vendor-financing) can address an invoice due before sales receipts arrive. When assessing **funding for ecommerce businesses** , confirm who receives the funds, which invoices qualify, and the repayment dates. Negotiate commercial terms with the vendor as well.


### Mixed operating costs


A Line of Credit can offer revolving access for changing expenses, subject to its terms. Compare draw costs, repayment frequency, and permitted uses. **Working capital loans for online sellers** can also provide a defined amount and repayment schedule; this[working capital loan guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/working-capital-loan-how-it-works) explains the mechanics.


### Stock purchases


**Ecommerce inventory financing** may fit businesses whose main constraint is buying stock. Review inventory eligibility, valuation, security requirements, and total cost. The[Inventory Financing guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/business-guide-for-inventory-financing) covers that structure in more detail.


Good **ecommerce business financing** should fit both the expense and the collection cycle. Include financing costs in product margins and test whether the business can repay if a launch underperforms.

## Frequently asked questions


### How much ecommerce working capital do I need?


Calculate the largest projected cash shortfall and add your chosen minimum cushion. Update the forecast for seasonality, returns, and repayment obligations.


### How do I fund an ecommerce business with uneven sales?


Start by mapping expenses and realistic collection dates. When deciding **how to fund an ecommerce business** , compare vendor terms, retained cash, and financing against that forecast.


### Can financing cover advertising and payroll?


Some facilities permit these operating uses. Confirm the agreement's restrictions before drawing funds; invoice-specific financing can have a narrower purpose.


### Will higher sales automatically improve cash flow?


Growth may require more inventory and marketing spending before receipts arrive. Recalculate the cash gap whenever order volume or reorder timing changes.
